AMI_SHARED_CROSS_ACCOUNT.description: The AMI's launch permission lists another account. Normalised account → AMI.

AWS_AUTH_MAPPING.description: aws-auth ConfigMap mapping (data only, never the raw ConfigMap).

CAN_ADMIN_KEY.description: PutKeyPolicy or CreateGrant (can grant itself decrypt); ScheduleKeyDeletion.

CAN_ADMIN_MSG.description: Change the topic or queue attributes or policy.

CAN_ADMIN_SG.description: Can change security-group rules (network exposure). Targets the SG (was the instance).

CAN_ASSUME.description: sts:AssumeRole is allowed by the role's trust policy and, where needed, the caller's identity policy (same-account root trust, cross-account, wildcard). Replaces CAN_ASSUME_CROSS.

CAN_ASSUME_WEB_IDENTITY.description: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity admitted by the trust policy; props.admits = any | pattern | specific.

CAN_DECRYPT.description: kms:Decrypt (key-policy-first evaluation). GenerateDataKey* alone is CAN_ENCRYPT.

CAN_ESCALATE.description: Self-escalation, or modification of a principal the source can already act as (closure, engine.md §4.6); evidence.chain lists the edge ids.

CAN_EXEC.description: Interactive execution inside running compute: ecs:ExecuteCommand, SageMaker presigned notebook or domain URLs.

CAN_HIJACK.description: A complete existing-resource chain (update plus run, with PassRole where needed) gives code execution as the resource's role.

CAN_MODIFY.description: Some compute-modifying action without a complete chain to code execution.

CAN_MODIFY_PERMISSIONS_OF.description: Put*/Attach*Policy, CreatePolicyVersion, SetDefaultPolicyVersion or boundary changes on another principal. Closure input: becomes CAN_ESCALATE when the target is reachable.

CAN_PASS_ROLE_TO.description: PassRole plus a service action that runs code as the passed role (new-passrole / existing-passrole rules); evidence.via lists the services, evidence.rule_ids the rules.

CAN_REACH_NODE_IMDS.description: The pod can reach the node's IMDS (hop limit, hostNetwork); Fargate excluded. evidence.weight_extra adds 0-2 by hop limit.

CAN_READ_SECRET.description: secretsmanager:GetSecretValue (BatchGet only with it). Metadata actions give no edge.

CAN_READ_TABLE.description: Read items, including PartiQL select and exports.

CAN_RUN_AS_SA.description: The role can create pods or tokens in the service account's namespace.

CAN_TAKEOVER.description: Credential or trust takeover of another principal: CreateAccessKey, Create/UpdateLoginProfile, UpdateAssumeRolePolicy, AddUserToGroup. Self is excluded.

CAN_UPDATE_CODE.description: lambda:UpdateFunctionCode: code execution as the execution role.

CAN_WRITE_SECRET.description: Update, put, delete, rotate or change the policy of the secret.

CLUSTER_ROLE.description: EKS control-plane service role; workloads never get it.

COGNITO_PUBLIC_IDENTITY.description: Anyone can get identities from the pool (AllowUnauth, or a public authenticated path).

DDB_GRANTS_CROSS_ACCOUNT.description: The table's resource policy grants another account. Normalised grantee → table.

EBS_SHARED_CROSS_ACCOUNT.description: createVolumePermission for another account. Normalised account → snapshot.

EBS_SHARED_PUBLIC.description: createVolumePermission for all. Normalised anonymous → snapshot.

EC2_FULL_ACCESS.description: ec2:* on the instance: user-data change plus stop/start gives code execution.

ECR_GRANTS_CROSS_ACCOUNT.description: The repository policy grants another account (pull or push). Normalised grantee → repository.

EKS_ACCESS_ENTRY.description: EKS access entry (and associated access policies) mapping the IAM principal into the cluster.

ENCRYPTED_BY.description: Default bucket encryption key (resolved KMS id).

EXPOSES.description: Internet-facing load balancer forwards to the target.

FULL_ACCESS.description: s3:* (identity policy or same-account bucket-policy grant).

GRANTS_PUBLIC.description: Public bucket policy or public ACL (BPA-aware). Normalised anonymous → bucket.

HAS_BOUNDARY.description: Managed policy used as the principal's permissions boundary.

HAS_POLICY.description: Managed policy attached to the principal (ARN-keyed).

INGRESS_ROUTES_TO.description: Ingress rule routes to the service. Renamed from the K8s EXPOSES.

INSTANCE_ROLE.description: Code on the instance gets the instance-profile role's credentials from IMDS. ARN-resolved; the dashboard's name-matched copy is removed.

INVOKES.description: API route proxies to the (unqualified) function.

IRSA_BRIDGE.description: IRSA: the annotated role trusts this service account through the cluster's OIDC provider.

IS_ADMIN_EQUIVALENT.description: The principal is admin-equivalent (ADMIN-001), so reaching it means reaching the account admin.

KMS_GRANT.description: A KMS grant whose operations include a decrypt-capable operation (grantee → key).

KMS_GRANTS_DECRYPT.description: The key policy names a same-account principal for decrypt. Normalised grantee → key.

LAMBDA_GRANTS_CROSS_ACCOUNT.description: The function policy lets another account invoke it. Normalised grantee → function.

LAMBDA_GRANTS_INVOKE.description: The function policy lets a same-account principal or service invoke it. Normalised grantee → function.

LAMBDA_GRANTS_PUBLIC.description: Public invoke (function policy or NONE-auth URL). Normalised anonymous → function.

LAYER_GRANTS_PUBLIC.description: The layer version policy grants everyone.

MEMBER_OF.description: The user inherits the group's grants; group capability edges start at the group node.

MSG_GRANTS_CROSS_ACCOUNT.description: The topic or queue policy grants another account. Normalised grantee → resource.

NODE_ROLE.description: Node instance role, reachable through node IMDS.

NOTIFIES.description: Bucket event notification: writing an object injects input, it does not give control.

POD_IDENTITY.description: EKS Pod Identity association whose role trusts pods.eks.amazonaws.com.

POOL_UNAUTH_ROLE.description: Unauthenticated identities get the role (emitted only when AllowUnauth is true).

PUBLIC_INBOUND.description: Reachable from the internet (security groups, routes, NACLs, scheme, endpoint access). INTERNET_FACING is folded into props.igw_routed.

RDS_SHARED_CROSS_ACCOUNT.description: The snapshot is shared with another account.

RUNS_AS.description: The pod mounts the service-account token (automount on).

SECRET_ENCRYPTED_BY.description: The secret's KMS key (default aws/secretsmanager resolved).

SECRET_GRANTS_CROSS_ACCOUNT.description: The secret's resource policy grants another account. Normalised grantee → secret.

SECRET_GRANTS_PUBLIC.description: The secret's resource policy grants everyone. Normalised anonymous → secret.

SELECTS.description: Service selector routes to the pod.

SERVICE_CAN_ASSUME.description: The trust policy admits an AWS service principal (PassRole candidates, confused-deputy checks).

SG_ALLOWS_FROM.description: Members of the source group can reach members of the target group.

SSMDOC_SHARED_CROSS_ACCOUNT.description: The SSM document's share permission lists another account. Normalised account → document.

SSMDOC_SHARED_PUBLIC.description: The SSM document is shared publicly.

SSRF_TO_IMDS.description: Public, running instance with IMDSv1 and a role: SSRF can read role credentials. Always conditional. Re-aimed from instance→role (dashboard) to anonymous→instance.

SUBSCRIBES.description: Topic subscription delivering to the endpoint.

USES_ROLE.description: The compute resource runs as the role (Lambda execution role, ECS task role, stack service role, job role). The ECS execution role is EXECUTION_ROLE.

VPC_CONNECTED.description: Network context: traffic can be routed between the two VPCs through an active VPC peering connection or a transit gateway both are attached to (evidence.via). Stored once per pair, smaller id first. VPN connections reaching a VPC are in its props.

evidence.trust_reason: the role's trust policy admits the service account

evaluation_gaps.detail: ECR repository or DynamoDB table policies that could not be read: their public or cross-account exposure is unknown, not absent.
Identity policies of external principals are not visible; cross-account edges are conditional.
KMS keys whose grants could not be listed: grant-based access to them is unknown, not absent.
Customer-managed KMS keys whose key policy could not be read: who may use them is evaluated as conditional (the key policy decides first).
reported by the evaluator while running the rules
RDS snapshots whose restore attribute could not be read: their public or cross-account sharing is unknown, not absent.
Condition values known only at request time (source IP, MFA, tags in the request) are not evaluated; such decisions are conditional.
Secret or parameter resource policies that could not be read: their public or cross-account exposure is unknown, not absent.
Session policies passed at AssumeRole time can only narrow permissions and are not modelled.

findings.description: Anyone can launch an instance from AMI 'ami-0dec0b0b11c000002' and read its volumes.
findings.remediation: Make the AMI private (remove the 'all' launch permission) and turn on AMI Block Public Access.
findings.title: AMI ami-0dec0b0b11c000002 is public

findings.description: Account 999999999999 can launch instances from AMI 'ami-0dec0000000000002' (launch permission).
findings.remediation: Verify the cross-account launch permission is intended.
findings.title: AMI ami-0dec0000000000002 is shared with account 999999999999

findings.description: These methods/routes have no effective authorisation (NONE): anyone who can reach the endpoint can invoke the Lambda function.
findings.remediation: Attach an authorizer (IAM, Cognito, JWT or Lambda) to the listed routes, or confirm that unauthenticated access is intended.
findings.title: API 'demo-http-api' has 1 Lambda route(s) without authentication

findings.description: These methods/routes have no effective authorisation (NONE): anyone who can reach the endpoint can invoke the Lambda function.
findings.remediation: Attach an authorizer (IAM, Cognito, JWT or Lambda) to the listed routes, or confirm that unauthenticated access is intended.
findings.title: API 'demo-rest-api' has 1 Lambda route(s) without authentication

findings.description: The dynamodb table's resource policy grants dynamodb:GetItem, dynamodb:Query to principals of account(s) 999999999999, independently of this account's IAM policies.
findings.remediation: Verify cross-account access is intended.
findings.title: DynamoDB table 'demo-orders' is shared with 999999999999

findings.description: The snapshot's createVolumePermission includes the 'all' group: anyone can create a volume from it and read the data.
findings.remediation: Remove the public createVolumePermission and set snapshot Block Public Access to block-all-sharing.
findings.title: EBS snapshot 'snap-0dec0b0b11c000021' is shared publicly

findings.description: Account 999999999999 can create volumes from the snapshot (createVolumePermission).
findings.remediation: Verify the cross-account sharing is intended.
findings.title: EBS snapshot 'snap-0dec054aaed000022' is shared with account 999999999999

findings.description: Instance 'i-0dec0eeb000000002' (running) has public address(es) 203.0.113.10; security group(s) sg-0dec0eeb000000002 admit 0.0.0.0/0 on 22/tcp.
findings.remediation: Restrict the security-group ingress to specific source ranges, or move the instance behind a load balancer in a private subnet.
findings.title: Instance i-0dec0eeb000000002 is reachable from the internet on 22/tcp

findings.description: Instance 'i-0dec0eeb000000002' (running) has HttpTokens 'optional' with the metadata endpoint enabled: SSRF can read the instance role's temporary credentials.
findings.remediation: Set HttpTokens to 'required' to enforce IMDSv2 (or disable the metadata endpoint).
findings.title: Instance i-0dec0eeb000000002 allows IMDSv1 (instance role exposed to SSRF)

findings.description: Instance 'i-0dec0eeb000000002' has public address(es) 203.0.113.10 and its subnet's effective route table routes to an attached internet gateway.
findings.remediation: Move the instance to a private subnet or remove its public address.
findings.title: Instance i-0dec0eeb000000002 has a public address in an internet-routed subnet

findings.description: The launch template 'demo-web-lt' has user data (content not collected). User data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute / DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions and through IMDS on the host; review it for embedded credentials.
findings.remediation: Review the user data for embedded credentials; move secrets to Secrets Manager or SSM SecureString parameters read at boot.
findings.title: User data is present on launch template demo-web-lt

findings.description: The registry permission policy grants replication or repository creation to principals outside this account, so they can place images in this registry.
findings.remediation: Remove registry-policy grants (ReplicateImage, CreateRepository) to accounts that should not write into this registry.
findings.title: ECR registry in eu-west-2 lets 999999999999 write images

findings.description: Registry replication rules copy images to registries of other accounts.
findings.remediation: Verify that cross-account replication destinations are intended and trusted.
findings.title: ECR images in eu-west-2 replicate to 999999999999

findings.description: The ecr repository's resource policy grants ecr:BatchGetImage, ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer to principals of account(s) 999999999999, independently of this account's IAM policies.
findings.remediation: Verify cross-account pull/push access is intended.
findings.title: ECR repository 'demo-api' is shared with 999999999999

findings.description: The access-entry mapping of arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/demo-admin-role gives it full control of cluster demo-cluster (access policy AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy). Whoever can use this IAM principal controls every workload, secret and service-account identity of the cluster.
findings.remediation: Review which IAM principals are mapped to system:masters or AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy; prefer namespaced access policies.
findings.title: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/demo-admin-role is a cluster administrator of EKS cluster demo-cluster

findings.description: The Kubernetes API endpoint of cluster demo-cluster (eu-west-2) is publicly accessible from 0.0.0.0/0. Authentication is still required, but any leaked kubeconfig, token or mapped IAM credential is usable from anywhere, and API-server vulnerabilities are exposed.
findings.remediation: Disable public endpoint access, or restrict publicAccessCidrs to known administration networks.
findings.title: EKS cluster demo-cluster has a public API endpoint open to the internet

findings.description: The load balancer scheme is 'internet-facing': its listeners are reachable from the internet and forward to its targets.
findings.remediation: Confirm the public exposure is intended; otherwise use an internal scheme, and protect it with a WAF web ACL.
findings.title: Load balancer 'demo-classic-elb' is internet-facing

findings.description: The load balancer scheme is 'internet-facing': its listeners (22/tcp, 443/tcp) are reachable from the internet and forward to its targets.
findings.remediation: Confirm the public exposure is intended; otherwise use an internal scheme, and protect it with a WAF web ACL.
findings.title: Load balancer 'demo-public-alb' is internet-facing

findings.description: SelfSubjectRulesReviews in 3 namespace(s) of cluster demo-cluster show: list secrets (reads every value), read secrets. They describe the identity the collector used, which is a foothold an attacker holding the same credentials would have.
findings.remediation: No action needed; review whether the collecting identity's Kubernetes rights are broader than intended.
findings.title: Kubernetes permissions of the collecting identity in cluster demo-cluster

findings.description: The pod shares the host's network namespace (every node interface, the node's IMDS).
findings.remediation: Remove hostNetwork: true.
findings.title: Pod uses hostNetwork (demo-apps/demo-worker-0, cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: The pod shares the host's network namespace (every node interface, the node's IMDS).
findings.remediation: Remove hostNetwork: true.
findings.title: Pod uses hostNetwork (kube-system/aws-node-xyz12, cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: The pod mounts directories of the node that give control of the node or its container runtime.
findings.remediation: Replace hostPath volumes by persistent volumes or projected sources; never mount the container runtime socket, the kubelet directory or the node's root filesystem.
findings.title: Pod mounts a hostPath volume (demo-apps/demo-worker-0, cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: The pod shares the host's PID namespace (it can see and signal every process on the node).
findings.remediation: Remove hostPID: true.
findings.title: Pod uses hostPID (demo-apps/demo-worker-0, cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: The pod-identity configuration of demo-apps/demo-worker names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/demo-app-role, but the role's trust policy does not admit it (trust policy: not_allowed (trust_policy)). The pods get no AWS credentials from it; the configuration is stale or was planted, and is not an attack path.
findings.remediation: Remove the stale eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation or Pod Identity association, or fix the role's trust policy if the workload needs it.
findings.title: Service account names an IAM role whose trust does not admit it (demo-apps/demo-worker, cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: The irsa configuration of kube-system/aws-node names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/demo-eks-node-role, but the role's trust policy does not admit it (trust policy: not_allowed (trust_policy)). The pods get no AWS credentials from it; the configuration is stale or was planted, and is not an attack path.
findings.remediation: Remove the stale eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation or Pod Identity association, or fix the role's trust policy if the workload needs it.
findings.title: Service account names an IAM role whose trust does not admit it (kube-system/aws-node, cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: Service demo-apps/demo-api-lb of type LoadBalancer gets an internet-facing AWS load balancer (in-tree cloud provider default (internet-facing)), open to any source address.
findings.remediation: Use an internal load balancer (service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-scheme: internal) or restrict loadBalancerSourceRanges.
findings.title: Service demo-apps/demo-api-lb is an internet-facing load balancer (cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: Ingress demo-apps/demo-api-ingress routes to demo-api-lb without an authentication annotation (alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internet-facing). Verify that the backends authenticate requests.
findings.remediation: Restrict the ingress or add authentication in front of it.
findings.title: Ingress demo-apps/demo-api-ingress has no authentication annotation (cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: A privileged container (regular, init or ephemeral) has every capability and the host's devices: it can take over the node.
findings.remediation: Remove privileged: true (regular, init and ephemeral containers).
findings.title: Privileged container (demo-apps/demo-worker-0, cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: ClusterRoleBinding 'demo-worker-admin' grants demo-apps/demo-worker every verb on every resource in the whole cluster. Every pod running as this service account controls the cluster.
findings.remediation: Use a more restrictive ClusterRole or a namespaced Role.
findings.title: ServiceAccount demo-apps/demo-worker bound to cluster-admin (cluster demo-cluster)

findings.description: StorageEncrypted is false: data at rest and its snapshots are not protected by KMS.
findings.remediation: Recreate the database (or restore an encrypted copy of a snapshot) with storage encryption.
findings.title: RDS instance 'demo-db' storage is not encrypted

findings.description: PubliclyAccessible is true: the endpoint resolves to a public address and is reachable from the internet wherever its security groups allow it.
findings.remediation: Set PubliclyAccessible=false and place the database in private subnets.
findings.title: RDS instance 'demo-db' is publicly accessible

findings.remediation: Remove public sharing from the snapshot immediately.
findings.title: RDS cluster snapshot 'demo-aurora-snap-public' is shared publicly

findings.description: The snapshot's restore attribute includes 'all': any AWS account can restore it and read the data.

findings.title: RDS snapshot 'demo-db-snap-public' is shared publicly

findings.description: Record 'www.example.com.' (CNAME) points at 'd111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net' (cloudfront, takeover info): cloudfront target (info to be claimable).
findings.remediation: Verify the target resource still exists and belongs to you; remove the record if not.

findings.description: Record 'old.example.com.' (CNAME) points at 'demo-old-site.s3-website-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com' (s3-website, takeover likely): no bucket 'demo-old-site' in this account: anyone may create it.

evidence.check: no bucket 'demo-old-site' in this account: anyone may create it

findings.remediation: Verify the target resource still exists and belongs to you; remove the record if not.

findings.description: S3 bucket 'demo-legacy-eu-bucket' gives anyone on the internet access (actions unknown: the policy could not be read); not verified: s3:GetBucketPolicy:denied.
findings.remediation: Remove the wildcard Principal or scope it with a principal-restricting condition (aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:SourceVpce, aws:SourceArn); keep Block Public Access (RestrictPublicBuckets) on at account level.
findings.title: Bucket 'demo-legacy-eu-bucket' is public according to AWS (policy not readable)

findings.description: S3 bucket 'demo-public-site' gives anyone on the internet CAN_READ (actions: s3:getobject).
findings.remediation: Remove the wildcard Principal or scope it with a principal-restricting condition (aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:SourceVpce, aws:SourceArn); keep Block Public Access (RestrictPublicBuckets) on at account level.
findings.title: Bucket 'demo-public-site' is public through its bucket policy (CAN_READ)

findings.description: S3 bucket 'demo-public-site' gives anyone on the internet CAN_READ.
findings.remediation: Remove the AllUsers / AuthenticatedUsers ACL grants, set Object Ownership to BucketOwnerEnforced (ACLs disabled) and turn on IgnorePublicAcls.
findings.title: Bucket 'demo-public-site' ACL grants anyone on the internet (READ)

findings.description: The secret's resource policy grants secretsmanager:GetSecretValue to any AWS principal.
findings.remediation: Remove the wildcard Principal or add a restrictive Condition (aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:PrincipalAccount).
findings.title: Secret 'demo_db-creds' is accessible to everyone through its resource policy

findings.description: The secret's resource policy grants secretsmanager:GetSecretValue to principals of account(s) 999999999999, independently of this account's IAM policies.
findings.remediation: Verify that cross-account access to the secret is intended; scope the Principal to specific role ARNs or add aws:PrincipalOrgID.
findings.title: Secret 'demo/db-creds' is shared with 999999999999

findings.description: The document's share permission includes 'all': any AWS account can read and run it; documents often embed scripts, endpoints and credentials.
findings.remediation: Stop sharing the document with 'all' (ssm:ModifyDocumentPermission) and review it for secrets.
findings.title: SSM document 'demo-run-shell' is shared publicly

findings.description: The document's share permission lists other accounts, which can read and run it.
findings.remediation: Verify that sharing the document with the listed accounts is intended.
findings.title: SSM document 'demo-patch-baseline' is shared with 999999999999

findings.description: The trust policy of 'demo-cross-account-role' allows 'arn:aws:iam::999999999999:root' from account 999999999999; guard: external-id.
findings.remediation: The trust requires sts:ExternalId; keep the value secret per customer and restrict the principal to the vendor's specific role ARN.
findings.title: Role 'demo-cross-account-role' trusts account 999999999999

findings.description: Web identity provider cognito-identity.amazonaws.com can assume 'demo-cognito-unauth-role'; cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr admits unauthenticated identities.
findings.remediation: Require the provider's audience (<host>:aud) and an exact subject (<host>:sub), e.g. repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/main for GitHub or system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa> for EKS.
findings.title: Role 'demo-cognito-unauth-role' trusts cognito identities (specific subjects)

findings.description: Web identity provider arn:aws:iam::111122223333:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/id/DEMO0000000000000000000000000002 can assume 'demo-irsa-role'.
findings.remediation: Require the provider's audience (<host>:aud) and an exact subject (<host>:sub), e.g. repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/main for GitHub or system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa> for EKS.
findings.title: Role 'demo-irsa-role' trusts eks identities (specific subjects)

findings.description: None of the logging trails has data-event selectors: S3 object reads/writes and Lambda invocations are not recorded.
findings.remediation: Add data-event selectors (S3 objects, Lambda invocations) for the sensitive resources.
findings.title: No CloudTrail trail records data events

findings.description: With the classic flow an identity can call AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity on any role whose trust policy admits this pool, bypassing the configured roles and mappings.
findings.remediation: Set AllowClassicFlow=false and make every role trust policy require the pool id (aud) and the expected amr.
findings.title: Cognito identity pool 'demo_identity_pool' allows the classic (basic) authentication flow

findings.description: With the classic flow an identity can call AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity on any role whose trust policy admits this pool, bypassing the configured roles and mappings.

findings.title: Cognito identity pool 'demo_roles_denied_pool' allows the classic (basic) authentication flow

findings.description: Access key AKIAEXAMPLEALICE0001 has not been rotated for 728 days (limit 90) and has not been used recently: deactivate it.
findings.remediation: Rotate the key (create a new one, switch, deactivate and delete the old one) or delete it if unused; prefer short-lived role credentials.
findings.title: IAM user 'demo-alice' has an active access key 728 days old

findings.description: No password policy is set: console passwords only need the AWS defaults (1 user(s) with a console password).
findings.remediation: Set an account password policy: length >= 14, all character classes, reuse prevention 24.
findings.title: The account has no IAM password policy

findings.description: A policy of the function lets arn:aws:iam::999999999999:root (account 999999999999) perform lambda:invokefunction.
findings.remediation: Verify cross-account invoke access is intended.
findings.title: Lambda 'demo-layered' grants access to account 999999999999

findings.description: The layer version policy lets any AWS account read the layer (lambda:GetLayerVersion): its code and any configuration or credentials packaged in it are exposed.
findings.remediation: Remove the public statement from the layer version policy (RemoveLayerVersionPermission) or restrict it to an organisation (aws:PrincipalOrgID).
findings.title: Lambda layer version 'demo-deps:3' is public

findings.description: The SNS policy lets arn:aws:iam::999999999999:root (account 999999999999) perform sns:publish.
findings.remediation: Verify cross-account access is intended.
findings.title: SNS 'demo-alerts' grants access to account 999999999999

findings.description: CloudFront distribution 'd222222abcdef8.cloudfront.net' is reachable from the internet and no AWS WAF web ACL inspects its requests.
findings.remediation: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL (managed rule groups for common exploits and bad inputs) with the endpoint.
findings.title: CloudFront distribution 'd222222abcdef8.cloudfront.net' has no WAF web ACL

findings.description: REST API 'demo-rest-auth' (stages dev) is reachable from the internet and no AWS WAF web ACL inspects its requests.
